blocks.text: The Parade of Champions at the Sambadrome

provenance.rationale: The title is taken from the approved Word itinerary paragraph and stripped of its Day 2 prefix.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, the day is free. We recommend sleeping in, enjoying a leisurely lunch, and allowing time to prepare for the nighttime parade.

By morning, more music and Carnival decorations are appearing around the city. Samba fills the streets, glitter and feathers appear in shop windows, and participants and spectators gradually gather near the Sambadrome.

In the evening, a transfer takes you to the Sambadrome for the program's highlight, the Parade of Champions. The top samba schools enter the avenue with their own themes, music, costumes, and enormous moving floats.

Each performance unfolds as a show in its own right. Thousands of dancers and musicians take part, while percussion ensembles set the rhythm for the entire Sambadrome. Floodlights, vibrant costumes, and elaborate scenery transform the avenue into a constantly moving stage.

The samba schools parade one after another. Each has its own colors, story, and musical theme, so the night becomes a succession of grand spectacles. The towering floats and large dance groups stretching across the full length of the parade avenue are especially impressive.

Over 10,000 dancers perform in a single night. The parade continues for many hours, ending late at night or even in the morning.

After the event, a transfer takes you from the Sambadrome back to your hotel.

blocks.text: Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer and Sunset at Arpoador

provenance.rationale: The Word itinerary names Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer and sunset at Arpoador in a single day.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, set off for Corcovado.

At the station, board an open train for the ascent through the tropical Tijuca Forest, one of the largest urban rainforests. Along the way, you will see vines, palms, ferns, and dense greenery that almost completely hides the city in some stretches. Occasionally, you may spot toucans, sloths, or monkeys near the route.

At the top of Corcovado stands the 38-meter statue of Christ the Redeemer. From the viewpoint, you can see how Rio stretches between the ocean, the lagoon, and granite mountains: neighborhoods climb the hillsides, patches of green forest remain close by, and beaches extend into the distance.

Many of the places you visited on previous days are visible again, now from a different angle: Sugarloaf Mountain, the bay, the beaches, and the districts around the lagoon. This is one of those places where Rio's geography makes sense when viewed from above.

After the main tour, you can spend time by the ocean. We recommend watching the sunset from the rocks of Arpoador, between Copacabana and Ipanema. Sit by the water and watch the sun sink behind the mountains as the shoreline and the ocean gradually change color.

For the evening, you may choose Marius, a seafood restaurant. The price is available on request.
